title: The exponential pullback represents maps over an object
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, coherent slices and homotopy pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a containing universe and a locally small quasicategory $\mathcal C$. Suppose $1$ is a terminal object, $a\in\mathcal C$, the products $T\times a$ exist for all $T$, and the coherent product functor $-\times a$ has a right adjoint $[a,-]$, meaning coherent equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,[a,z])\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T\times a,z)$ natural in $T,z$. Let $p:y\to a$, let $e:1\to[a,a]$ correspond to $\mathrm{id}_a:1\times a\simeq a\to a$, and suppose the following homotopy pullback exists in $\mathcal C$:
$$P_p=1\times^h_{[a,a]}[a,y],$$
where $[a,y]\to[a,a]$ is $[a,p]$. Evaluation and the specified pullback homotopy induce equivalences of full mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,P_p)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\operatorname{pr}_a}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T\times a,y)\xrightarrow{p\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T\times a,a)\bigr)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{/a}}((T\times a,\operatorname{pr}_a),(y,p)).$$
The equivalences are coherently natural in $T$ and in maps $p\to p'$ in $\mathcal C_{/a}$ for which the displayed pullbacks exist, and retain all simplicial parameters. In particular, transposition carries the point $e\circ!$ to the product projection $\operatorname{pr}_a$ and carries postcomposition by $[a,p]$ to postcomposition by $p$.

proof.text: Put $A_T=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,[a,y])$, $B_T=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,[a,a])$ and $E_T=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,1)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] to the assumed pullback cone (its indexing span is finite). It identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,P_p)$ with $A_T\times^h_{B_T}E_T$, where the maps are postcomposition by $[a,p]$ and $e$. By terminality, $E_T$ is contractible. Choose its terminal arrow $!_T$ and insert the point $\{!_T\}\to E_T$. This is a weak equivalence; the other two maps of the resulting spans are identities. Thus [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] identifies $\operatorname{hofib}_{e!_T}(A_T\to B_T)$ with $A_T\times^h_{B_T}E_T$. All spaces involved are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The inverse comparison gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,P_p)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{e!_T}(A_T\to B_T)$. In the path model this comparison retains the map to $[a,y]$ and the pullback compatibility path; terminality removes only the contractible choice of the arrow to $1$.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.13: representability of maps from the product-to-slice functor; explicit mapping-space argument by the worker, using only the pullbacks and exponential adjunction assumed in the statement.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_{T,z}:\operatorname{Map}(T,[a,z])\simeq\operatorname{Map}(T\times a,z)$ for the specified adjunction equivalences. Their given naturality in $z$ supplies the coherent square
$$\alpha_{T,a}\circ([a,p]\circ-)\simeq(p\circ-)\circ\alpha_{T,y}.$$
Their naturality in $T$, applied to $!_T:T\to1$, gives
$$\alpha_{T,a}(e!_T)\simeq\alpha_{1,a}(e)\circ(!_T\times\mathrm{id}_a)=\mathrm{id}_a\circ\operatorname{pr}_a=\operatorname{pr}_a,$$
using $1\times a\simeq a$ and the definition of $e$. These are substitutions in the assumed coherent natural equivalence, so they also hold for every simplicial family of maps, rather than just on components.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.13: representability of maps from the product-to-slice functor; explicit mapping-space argument by the worker, using only the pullbacks and exponential adjunction assumed in the statement.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to the square in step 2 with horizontal maps $\alpha_{T,y}$ and $\alpha_{T,a}$. Both horizontal maps are equivalences, and the square carries exactly the specified naturality homotopy. Its forward implication therefore makes the induced map on each homotopy fiber an equivalence. At the point $e!_T$, use the path $\alpha_{T,a}(e!_T)\simeq\operatorname{pr}_a$ from step 2 to obtain
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{e!_T}([a,p]\circ-)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\operatorname{pr}_a}(p\circ-).$$
Concretely $(u,\gamma:[a,p]u\simeq e!_T)$ goes to $\alpha_{T,y}(u)$ with the path obtained by the naturality homotopy, $\alpha_{T,a}(\gamma)$, and the final path to $\operatorname{pr}_a$. The cited fiber theorem retains higher simplices and allows empty fibers; it requires no fibration hypothesis on postcomposition. Composing with step 1 proves the first equivalence in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.13: representability of maps from the product-to-slice functor; explicit mapping-space argument by the worker, using only the pullbacks and exponential adjunction assumed in the statement.

proof.text:
Specialize [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to the one-point shape $K=\Delta^0$ and diagram with value $a$. Its coherent cone category is $\mathcal C_{/a}$, since a cone is just an arrow to $a$ with its coherent triangles. Take its two cones to be $\operatorname{pr}_a:T\times a\to a$ and $p:y\to a$. The cited mapping-space formula reads
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{/a}}((T\times a,\operatorname{pr}_a),(y,p))\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\operatorname{pr}_a}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T\times a,y)\xrightarrow{p\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T\times a,a)\bigr).$$
Invert it to get the second required equivalence. The underlying arrow is the evaluation of $u:T\to[a,y]$; its homotopy over $a$ is precisely the path described in step 3.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.13: representability of maps from the product-to-slice functor; explicit mapping-space argument by the worker, using only the pullbacks and exponential adjunction assumed in the statement.

proof.text: For clarity, coherence in the varying object $p$ does not require independent choices of arrows between pullbacks. Let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_{/a}$ send $T$ to $(T\times a,\operatorname{pr}_a)$, and let $D_0$ be the full subcategory of objects $p$ for which the assumed pullback exists. Evaluation gives a map $P_p\times a\to y$; the pullback path and step 2 give its triangle over $a$, hence a map $\epsilon_p:G(P_p)\to p$. Steps 1–4 show that postcomposition with this map induces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,P_p)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{/a}}(G(T),p)$: it sends $v:T\to P_p$ to evaluation after $(\pi_{[a,y]}v)\times\mathrm{id}_a$, with the displayed triangle. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] hold for $G$ and $D_0$. That lemma assembles these universal arrows coherently, with contractible choice, and gives their mapping-space equivalences for every simplicial parameter $K$, compatibly with restriction in $K$. For an arrow $h:p\to p'$ its induced map $P_p\to P_{p'}$ is the one given by $[a,h]$ and the triangle $p'h\simeq p$: on a test map it sends $(u,\gamma)$ to $([a,h]u,\gamma')$, and after evaluation to $(h\alpha(u),\alpha(\gamma'))$. Naturality of $\alpha$ identifies these two descriptions, including the triangle paths. The representable-limit equivalences are natural in testing objects and diagrams by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. These identifications prove the claimed coherent naturality of the actual pullback/evaluation comparison in both variables and all simplicial parameters.
